newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BAYERN MUNICH PEN PICTURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BAYERN MUNICH PEN PICTURES.

text.p: Pen pictures of the probable Bayern Munich team and the referee for Sunday's German first division match against VfB Stuttgart:

Oliver Kahn. Goalkeeper. Age 27. Germany's second-choice goalkeeper who is ambitious to make a career in the national team. Huge man at 1.88 metres who dominates the penalty area with both his stature and loud voice.

Lothar Matthaeus. Libero. Age 35. Germany's most capped player with 122 internationals and a former World Cup captain. His international days now look over and did not go to England with Euro 96 squad. He is slower than in his heyday but still a player who can turn a match with a deft piece of skill. May return to his midfield role.
Samuel Kuffour. Defender. Age 20. Ghanaian international who came from Nuremberg this year and who has impressed the Bavarians.
Thomas Helmer. Defender. Age 31. Key part of Germany's Euro 96 team, Helmer is strong in the air and good at free kick situations. One goal this season.

Mario Basler. Midfielder. Age 27. Joined from Werder Bremen at start of season. The German international has promised a great deal in recent seasons but injuries have often hindered his progress. One of the country's most gifted players but his comments in public often get him into trouble. Scored three times this season, twice last weekend (one from penalty).

Thomas Strunz. Midfielder. Age 28. Versatile German international who is a good player at the back but who can also go forward. Injuries have hindered his form in recent seasons. Former Stuttgart player. One goal this season.

Dieter Hamann, midfielder. Age 23. Been at club since he joined from local club in 1989. He was sent off in the 30th minute of last year's corresponding game for foul on Stuttgart striker Giovane Elber. One goal so far.
Christian Nerlinger. Midfielder. Age 23. One of Bayern's rising stars who has been at the club since 1987 and who fits into the team well alongside the bigger names. One goal this season.

Christian Ziege. Wing back. 24. Several Italian clubs keen to get the German international's signature and good chance he will leave at the end of the season. Operates down the left-hand flank. Three goals so far.

Juergen Klinsmann. Forward. Age 32. Germany's captain and most well-known player has scored four times this season -- Bayern's top scorer. The former Tottenham player remains one of the most dangerous strikers in the game. First made his name in a VfB Stuttgart shirt.

Alexander Zickler. Forward. Age 22. Former Dynamo Dresden player came under fire for his lack of sharpness in front of goal when he was thrown into the team because of injuries two seasons ago but has matured into a good partner for Klinsmann. Impressed national coach Berti Vogts at this week's session for prospective internationals. Three goals so far.
Referee: Hartmut Strampe (Handorf). Age 40. Has been operating in the Bundesliga since 1991 and FIFA referee since 1993.
